name: Short Put Condor
summary: Sell the outer puts and buy the two middle puts for a net credit; long-volatility payoff built entirely in puts.
max_profit: net credit x 100, outside A and D
max_loss: (W1 - net credit) x 100, between B and C
when_to_use: Low IV rank (<= 25) breakout expectation, when put-side pricing beats the reverse iron condor. Otherwise use the reverse iron condor.
entry_rules: Breakout distance to A or D <= 1.0 x expected move
OI >= 500, spread <= 10% of mid on all legs
Alpaca level 3 (each short is covered by a long at a strike that bounds the risk)
management_rules: Take profit at 60% of max profit
Loss stop at 50% of max loss
Close within 30 minutes of the open after a scheduled catalyst
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
Short put D is ITM from entry: close the structure if D's extrinsic < $0.10 or its delta <= -0.90
Close when spot moves beyond A or above D by 0.5 x W1 (near max profit)
assignment_risk: High: short put D is ITM at entry and assignment means buying 100 shares per contract at strike D. Prefer the reverse iron condor, which keeps all shorts OTM.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 per leg; ITM puts must be quotable.
common_mistakes: Carrying the ITM short put; mistaking the credit for premium income.
zero_dte_notes: Avoid - ITM short put on expiration day.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
